Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines: IP indemnity notice routing and evidence SLA

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, please find attached our marked-up MSA and a short evidence checklist that the customer counsel asked us to confirm. The primary open item from legal is how the liability cap carve-out for IP infringement should be scoped and how notice/evidence routing will work operationally.

Two concrete asks to unblock the Order Form:
- Confirm you are okay with a liability-cap carve-out that applies solely to amounts payable under an IP indemnity obligation (i.e., excludes consequential and punitive damages but is not unlimited).
- Confirm the notice and evidence SLA: Redwood requests notice within 15 business days of becoming aware; Greenfield has proposed 30 calendar days. We also need to confirm the point of contact for receiving infringement notices and whether they will accept our evidence checklist (attached).

Proposed carve-out language we think is reasonable: (please review; legal has redlines below)

"Notwithstanding the limitations set forth in Section 8 (Limitation of Liability) above, the liability cap shall not apply to (i) amounts awarded in a final judgment by a court of competent jurisdiction for third-party claims for infringement of a third party's patents, copyrights or trademarks to the extent such claims arise from Customer's use of the Services, and (ii) amounts Redwood is obligated to pay under Section 9 (IP Indemnity), provided that Redwood's liability for such IP indemnity obligations shall be limited to direct damages actually incurred and shall exclude punitive, incidental, and consequential damages. Customer must provide prompt written notice of any alleged infringement and provide Redwood the opportunity, at Redwood's expense, to defend or settle the claim."

If you prefer alternative phrasing (e.g., a narrower trigger tied to specific model versions, or an escrow mechanism), flag that and we will route to Contracts.

Attachments: MSA_Redline_20280821.pdf, evidence_checklist.xlsx

Best,

Thanks for the redline and checklist. We reviewed briefly with our in-house counsel and looped in our outside counsel (Simpson & Lee) for the IP carveout. A few items from Greenfield's side:

- We are reluctant to accept an open-ended carve-out tied only to an indemnity promise. Our preference is either (A) a carve-out capped at the total Fees paid in the prior 12 months for the affected Service, or (B) a carve-out limited to direct damages but with a minimum floor to ensure recoverability.
- Notice timing: 30 calendar days from Customer discovery is our starting ask; we can accept 15 business days only if Redwood confirms the primary contact and a 24/7 escalation channel for suspected infringements.
- Evidence: we attached our counsel's suggested evidence list (Greenfield_Comments_20280821.docx). They also asked whether Redwood requires source code escrow or other mitigation — we said we would confirm.

Marissa / Aditya —

Thanks for flagging. Quick internal take from Contracts & IP: we can accept a carve-out limited to IP indemnity obligations but need to tighten the trigger and evidence obligations to avoid open-ended exposure. High-level proposed edits below (we should table to AC for final sign-off):

1) Narrowed trigger: Replace "to the extent such claims arise from Customer's use of the Services" with "to the extent such claims arise solely from Redwood's delivery or operation of the Services and not from Customer modifications, Customer data, or Customer-provided prompts or models."

2) Monetary boundary: Use a two-tier approach rather than unlimited exposure: Redwood's liability under the IP indemnity carve-out shall be limited to the lesser of (a) direct damages awarded in a final judgment and (b) an amount equal to the total Fees paid by Customer under the Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim, except where a court awards greater damages for willful infringement.

3) Notice & evidence: Customer must (i) give written notice within 15 business days of discovery, (ii) provide the evidence checklist (see attached) within 10 business days of notice, and (iii) permit Redwood to assume defense within 30 days. If Customer fails to provide the required evidence in that timeframe, Redwood may seek dismissal of the indemnity obligation on grounds of material prejudice.

Proposed redline snippet to paste into the MSA: 
"For clarity, the liability cap set forth in Section 8 shall not apply to liabilities arising from claims for infringement by third parties to the extent such liabilities are solely attributable to Redwood's Services (as used pursuant to the Order Form). Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood's aggregate monetary exposure under such IP indemnity obligations shall not exceed the lesser of (i) direct damages finally awarded by a court of competent jurisdiction and (ii) the total Fees paid by Customer under the applicable Order Form in the 12 months prior to the claim, except in cases of willful infringement. Customer shall provide prompt written notice (no later than 15 business days from discovery), deliver the evidence checklist within 10 business days of notice, and permit Redwood to control the defense and settlement of the claim. Failure to provide required evidence within the stated period shall relieve Redwood of defense and indemnity obligations to the extent Redwood is materially prejudiced."

Questions for Sales: do you want to push for removing the 12-month fees cap (commercial ask) or accept this as a compromise? Also confirm whether Greenfield will accept our assumption of defense and whether they insist on any escrow/mitigation.

-Laura
